case_name: Sri Dhruba Borthakur vs Smt Barnali Goswami
facts_of_case: Petitioner husband had instituted F.C.(Civil) 203/2013 under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 before the Court. The proceeding resulted in the judgment dated 12.10.2018 by which the petition for a dissolution of marriage stood dismissed.

legal_principles.principle: An application for dissolution of marriage under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 requires an adjudication and a satisfaction to be arrived at by the Court granting dissolution of the marriage.
legal_principles.held: As there is a further requirement of the Court to go into certain questions and arrive at its satisfaction, we are of the view that it would be more appropriate for the parties to file a petition under Section 13(B) of the Act of 1955 before the District Court.

legal_principles.principle: A petition for dissolution of marriage by a decree of divorce may be presented to the District Court by both parties together, whether such marriage was solemnized before or after the commencement of the Marriage Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976.
legal_principles.held: Subject to the provisions of this Act a petition for dissolution of marriage by a decree of divorce may be presented to the district court by both the parties to a marriage together, whether such marriage was solemnized before or after the commencement of the Marriage Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976 (68 of 1976).

outcome.final_order: The respondent is agreeable to go for dissolution, and what remains to be decided between the parties is for arriving at an appropriate permanent alimony that may be agreed upon.
